subject.title: Feature: Subscribe to WhatsApp call events (Baileys)

question: What WhatsApp call-event metadata should OpenClaw expose, retain, and make visible to agents or plugins for inbound Baileys `call` events?
rationale: Baileys call events carry contact identifiers, call status/timing, and group context, while the issue leaves open whether this should be session metadata, a tool, a plugin hook, or another event surface.

options.title: Opt-in sanitized activity events
options.body: Add a default-off WhatsApp-plugin setting or hook that emits sanitized call activity after existing account/access-control filtering and documents retention/exposure boundaries.

options.title: Minimal last-contact signal only
options.body: Record only a bounded last-contact activity signal for authorized chats and avoid exposing raw call payloads to agents or plugins.

options.title: Decline call tracking
options.body: Keep WhatsApp call metadata outside OpenClaw until the channel has a stronger privacy model for non-message activity.

recommendation.title: Opt-in sanitized activity events
recommendation.body: Add a default-off WhatsApp-plugin setting or hook that emits sanitized call activity after existing account/access-control filtering and documents retention/exposure boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest recent WhatsApp/plugin-area history signal and already scoped both this issue and the adjacent outbound-call distinction.
